```{=html}
    <input id="ks-rep" type="range" min="0" max="50" value="10" style="width:100%;" />
  </div>
</div>
<canvas id="ks-canvas" width="860" height="400" style="width:100%; border:1px solid #eee; border-radius:4px; background:#fafafa;"></canvas>
<div id="ks-legend" style="padding:10px; background:#e8f5e9; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; margin-top:10px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  var $ = function(id) { return document.getElementById(id); };

  function poissonPMF(k, lambda) {
    if (lambda <= 0) return k === 0 ? 1 : 0;
    var logP = k * Math.log(lambda) - lambda;
    for (var i = 2; i <= k; i++) logP -= Math.log(i);
    return Math.exp(logP);
  }

  function negBinomPMF(k, mean, variance) {
    if (mean <= 0 || variance <= mean) return poissonPMF(k, mean);
    var r = (mean * mean) / (variance - mean);
    var p = 1 - mean / variance;
    var logP = 0;
    for (var i = 0; i < k; i++) logP += Math.log(r + i) - Math.log(i + 1);
    logP += r * Math.log(1 - p) + k * Math.log(p);
    return Math.exp(logP);
  }

  function draw() {
    var C = parseInt($('ks-cov').value);
    var errRate = parseInt($('ks-err').value) / 10;
    var hetRate = parseInt($('ks-het').value) / 10;
    var repFrac = parseInt($('ks-rep').value) / 100;

    $('ks-cov-val').textContent = C;
    $('ks-err-val').textContent = errRate.toFixed(1);
    $('ks-het-val').textContent = hetRate.toFixed(1);
    $('ks-rep-val').textContent = Math.round(repFrac * 100);

    var maxX = Math.min(Math.round(C * 4), 300);
    var spectrum = new Array(maxX + 1);
    for (var i = 0; i <= maxX; i++) spectrum[i] = 0;

    var genomeSize = 10000;
    var k = 21;
    var totalKmers = genomeSize;

    var errKmers = errRate * 0.01 * k * totalKmers * C;
    var hetKmers = hetRate * 0.01 * totalKmers;
    var repKmers2 = repFrac * 0.5 * totalKmers;
    var repKmers3 = repFrac * 0.3 * totalKmers;
    var repKmers4 = repFrac * 0.2 * totalKmers;
    var homoKmers = totalKmers - hetKmers - repKmers2 - repKmers3 - repKmers4;
    if (homoKmers < 0) homoKmers = totalKmers * 0.5;

    var variance = C * 1.3;

    for (var x = 1; x <= maxX; x++) {
      var errContrib = errKmers * Math.exp(-x * 1.5);
      var hetContrib = hetKmers * negBinomPMF(x, C / 2, C / 2 * 1.3);
      var homoContrib = homoKmers * negBinomPMF(x, C, variance);
      var rep2Contrib = repKmers2 * negBinomPMF(x, 2 * C, 2 * variance);
      var rep3Contrib = repKmers3 * negBinomPMF(x, 3 * C, 3 * variance);
      var rep4Contrib = repKmers4 * negBinomPMF(x, 4 * C, 4 * variance);
      spectrum[x] = errContrib + hetContrib + homoContrib + rep2Contrib + rep3Contrib + rep4Contrib;
    }

    var canvas = $('ks-canvas');
    var ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
    var W = canvas.width;
    var H = canvas.height;
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);

    var marginL = 70, marginR = 30, marginT = 40, marginB = 50;
    var plotW = W - marginL - marginR;
    var plotH = H - marginT - marginB;

    // Compute component arrays
    var errVals = [], hetVals = [], homoVals = [], repVals = [];
    for (var x = 0; x <= maxX; x++) {
      errVals[x] = errKmers * Math.exp(-x * 1.5);
      hetVals[x] = hetKmers * negBinomPMF(x, C / 2, C / 2 * 1.3);
      homoVals[x] = homoKmers * negBinomPMF(x, C, variance);
      repVals[x] = repKmers2 * negBinomPMF(x, 2 * C, 2 * variance) +
                   repKmers3 * negBinomPMF(x, 3 * C, 3 * variance) +
                   repKmers4 * negBinomPMF(x, 4 * C, 4 * variance);
    }

    // Log-scale Y-axis: find range from all values >= 1
    var minLogY = Infinity, maxLogY = -Infinity;
    for (var x = 1; x <= maxX; x++) {
      if (spectrum[x] > 0.5) {
        var ly = Math.log10(spectrum[x]);
        if (ly < minLogY) minLogY = ly;
        if (ly > maxLogY) maxLogY = ly;
      }
    }
    if (minLogY === Infinity) { minLogY = 0; maxLogY = 1; }
    // Round to nice tick boundaries
    minLogY = Math.floor(minLogY);
    maxLogY = Math.ceil(maxLogY + 0.3);
    var logRange = maxLogY - minLogY;
    if (logRange < 1) logRange = 1;

    // Draw axes
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#333';
    ctx.lineWidth = 1;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(marginL, marginT);
    ctx.lineTo(marginL, marginT + plotH);
    ctx.lineTo(marginL + plotW, marginT + plotH);
    ctx.stroke();

    ctx.fillStyle = '#333';
    ctx.font = '12px Arial';
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    ctx.fillText('K-mer multiplicity', marginL + plotW / 2, H - 8);
    ctx.save();
    ctx.translate(16, marginT + plotH / 2);
    ctx.rotate(-Math.PI / 2);
    ctx.fillText('Number of distinct k-mers (log scale)', 0, 0);
    ctx.restore();
    ctx.font = 'bold 13px Arial';
    ctx.fillText('Simulated K-mer Frequency Histogram', W / 2, 22);

    var xScale = plotW / maxX;

    // Y mapping: log10(value) -> pixel
    function yPx(val) {
      if (val <= 0) return marginT + plotH + 10; // off-screen below
      var ly = Math.log10(val);
      var frac = (ly - minLogY) / logRange;
      return marginT + plotH - frac * plotH;
    }

    // Draw Y-axis grid lines and tick labels
    ctx.font = '10px Arial';
    ctx.fillStyle = '#666';
    ctx.textAlign = 'right';
    for (var exp = minLogY; exp <= maxLogY; exp++) {
      var py = marginT + plotH - ((exp - minLogY) / logRange) * plotH;
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.strokeStyle = '#e0e0e0';
      ctx.moveTo(marginL, py);
      ctx.lineTo(marginL + plotW, py);
      ctx.stroke();
      var label = exp <= 0 ? '1' : '10';
      if (exp > 1) label = '10^' + exp;
      else if (exp === 1) label = '10';
      else if (exp === 0) label = '1';
      else label = '10^' + exp;
      ctx.fillText(label, marginL - 6, py + 4);
    }

    function drawComponent(vals, color, alpha) {
      ctx.save();
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.rect(marginL, marginT, plotW, plotH);
      ctx.clip();
      ctx.strokeStyle = color;
      ctx.lineWidth = 1.5;
      ctx.globalAlpha = alpha;
      ctx.beginPath();
      var started = false;
      for (var x = 1; x <= maxX; x++) {
        if (vals[x] <= 0) continue;
        var px = marginL + x * xScale;
        var py = yPx(vals[x]);
        if (!started) { ctx.moveTo(px, py); started = true; } else ctx.lineTo(px, py);
      }
      ctx.stroke();
      ctx.globalAlpha = 1.0;
      ctx.restore();
    }

    drawComponent(errVals, '#ff5722', 0.5);
    drawComponent(hetVals, '#9c27b0', 0.5);
    drawComponent(homoVals, '#2196F3', 0.5);
    drawComponent(repVals, '#4CAF50', 0.5);

    // Draw total spectrum
    ctx.save();
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.rect(marginL, marginT, plotW, plotH);
    ctx.clip();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#333';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.beginPath();
    var started = false;
    for (var x = 1; x <= maxX; x++) {
      if (spectrum[x] <= 0) continue;
      var px = marginL + x * xScale;
      var py = yPx(spectrum[x]);
      if (!started) { ctx.moveTo(px, py); started = true; } else ctx.lineTo(px, py);
    }
    ctx.stroke();
    ctx.restore();

    // Labels
    function drawLabel(text, xPos, color) {
      if (xPos < 1 || xPos > maxX) return;
      var val = spectrum[Math.round(xPos)];
      if (val <= 0) return;
      var px = marginL + xPos * xScale;
      var py = yPx(val) - 12;
      if (py < marginT + 15) py = marginT + 15;
      ctx.fillStyle = color;
      ctx.font = 'bold 11px Arial';
      ctx.textAlign = 'center';
      ctx.fillText(text, px, py);
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.setLineDash([3, 3]);
      ctx.strokeStyle = color;
      ctx.lineWidth = 1;
      ctx.moveTo(px, marginT + plotH);
      ctx.lineTo(px, py + 4);
      ctx.stroke();
      ctx.setLineDash([]);
    }

    drawLabel('Errors', 2, '#ff5722');
    if (hetRate > 0.2) drawLabel('Het (~' + Math.round(C / 2) + 'x)', Math.round(C / 2), '#9c27b0');
    drawLabel('Homo (~' + C + 'x)', C, '#2196F3');
    if (repFrac > 0.02) drawLabel('2C', 2 * C, '#4CAF50');

    // X-axis ticks
    ctx.font = '10px Arial';
    ctx.fillStyle = '#666';
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    var tickStep = Math.max(1, Math.round(maxX / 10));
    for (var x = 0; x <= maxX; x += tickStep) {
      var px = marginL + x * xScale;
      ctx.fillText(x, px, marginT + plotH + 16);
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.strokeStyle = '#ccc';
      ctx.moveTo(px, marginT + plotH);
      ctx.lineTo(px, marginT + plotH + 4);
      ctx.stroke();
    }

    $('ks-legend').innerHTML =
      '<span style="color:#ff5722; font-weight:bold;">--- Error peak</span> | ' +
      '<span style="color:#9c27b0; font-weight:bold;">--- Heterozygous peak (C/2)</span> | ' +
      '<span style="color:#2196F3; font-weight:bold;">--- Homozygous peak (C)</span> | ' +
      '<span style="color:#4CAF50; font-weight:bold;">--- Repeat peaks (2C, 3C, ...)</span> | ' +
      '<span style="font-weight:bold;">--- Total spectrum</span>';
  }

  $('ks-cov').addEventListener('input', draw);
  $('ks-err').addEventListener('input', draw);
  $('ks-het').addEventListener('input', draw);
  $('ks-rep').addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

### GenomeScope: Genome Profiling from K-mers

**GenomeScope** ([Vurture et al., *Bioinformatics* 2017](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btx153)) fits a mixture model to the k-mer frequency histogram to estimate:

- **Genome size**: Total number of unique k-mers divided by the average coverage
- **Heterozygosity**: Ratio of the heterozygous peak to the homozygous peak
- **Repeat fraction**: Area under the high-frequency tail

The model assumes k-mers are sampled from the genome following a negative binomial distribution (to account for coverage variation). **GenomeScope 2.0** ([Ranallo-Benavidez et al., *Nature Communications* 2020](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-14998-3)) extended this to polyploid genomes.

:::{.callout-note}
## Genome Size Estimation
The formula for genome size from k-mer counting is elegantly simple:

$$G = \frac{N}{C}$$

where $N$ is the total number of k-mers (after error removal) and $C$ is the average k-mer coverage (the position of the homozygous peak). This works because each base in the genome is covered by approximately $C$ k-mers. In practice, GenomeScope fits a negative binomial mixture model to the spectrum to estimate these parameters more precisely, but the core intuition is this simple ratio.
:::

### Merqury: Assembly Quality Assessment

**Merqury** ([Rhie et al., *Genome Biology* 2020](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-020-02134-9)) uses k-mer set operations to evaluate genome assemblies **without a reference**:

- **Spectra-asm plot**: Which read k-mers are found in the assembly? Missing k-mers indicate gaps; extra k-mers indicate errors.
- **QV estimation**: The fraction of k-mers in the assembly not found in the reads gives an estimated base-level quality score.
- **Hap-mers**: K-mers unique to one haplotype enable phasing assessment.

:::{.callout-important}
## Key Insight
The k-mer frequency histogram is like a fingerprint for your sequencing data. Before running any assembly or alignment, examining it tells you fundamental properties of your genome -- size, ploidy, repeat content, error rate -- and helps you choose appropriate parameters for downstream analysis.
:::

---

## 4. The Scaling Problem

We have seen that k-mers are powerful tools for genome analysis. But there is a problem: **storing all k-mers does not scale**.

Consider indexing the human genome with 15-mers:

| Quantity | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Genome length | $3 \times 10^9$ bp |
| Number of 15-mers | ~$3 \times 10^9$ |
| Bytes per entry (k-mer + position) | ~12 bytes |
| Total index size | ~36 GB |

This is manageable for a single genome. But what about mapping long reads? A 10 kb read generates ~10,000 k-mers. Each must be looked up in the index. With millions of reads, we need billions of lookups.

For more complex tasks -- like all-vs-all comparison of reads for overlap detection in genome assembly -- the situation is worse. With $N$ reads, we need $O(N^2)$ comparisons, each involving many k-mer lookups.

:::{.callout-important}
## Key Insight
We do not need to index **every** k-mer. If we can select a **representative subset** of k-mers that still covers the genome densely enough to find all true matches, we can dramatically reduce index size and lookup time. This is the key idea behind **minimizers**.
:::

---

## 5. Minimizers

**Minimizers** ([Roberts et al., *Bioinformatics* 2004](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/bth408)) provide an elegant solution to the scaling problem. The idea is simple: instead of using every k-mer as a seed, select only the **smallest** k-mer within each window of consecutive k-mers.

### Definition

Given parameters:
- $k$: the k-mer size
- $w$: the window size (number of consecutive k-mers in each window)

A **minimizer** is the lexicographically smallest k-mer among $w$ consecutive k-mers. As the window slides by one position, the minimizer may stay the same or change.

For a sequence of length $L$:
- Total k-mers: $L - k + 1$
- Total windows of $w$ consecutive k-mers: $L - k - w + 2$
- Each window selects exactly one minimizer (the smallest k-mer in it)

### Why Minimizers Work

The key property: **if two sequences share a substring of length $w + k - 1$, they must share at least one minimizer**. This is because they share $w$ consecutive k-mers, and the minimum of those k-mers must be the same.

This guarantee means minimizers preserve matching sensitivity while dramatically reducing the number of seeds:

| Approach | Seeds per genome | Relative size |
|----------|-----------------|---------------|
| Every k-mer | $n$ | 1x |
| Every w-th k-mer | $n/w$ | $1/w$ (but misses matches) |
| Minimizers (window $w$) | ~$2n/(w+1)$ | ~$2/(w+1)$ (no missed matches) |

The **density** of minimizers -- the fraction of k-mers selected -- approaches $2/(w+1)$ in random sequences. With $w = 10$, this means only about 18% of k-mers are kept, an **82% reduction** in index size with no loss of matching sensitivity.

:::{.callout-tip}
## Quick Intuition
Think of minimizers as street addresses for sequence regions. Rather than describing every nucleotide, you pick a few landmark k-mers that let you rapidly find where two sequences might align — then do the expensive exact comparison only there.
:::

:::{.callout-note}
## Practical Window Sizes
Minimap2 uses $k = 15$ and $w = 10$ for long reads, and $k = 21$ and $w = 11$ for short reads. The [Kraken 2](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-019-1891-0) metagenomic classifier stores minimizers of length 7 extracted from 31-mers (rather than storing the full 31-mers), achieving an **85% memory reduction** compared to [Kraken 1](https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46).
:::

```{=html}

<div id="viz-minimizer" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Interactive Minimizer Selection Demo</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">See how minimizers are selected: the lexicographically smallest k-mer in each window of w consecutive k-mers. Minimizers are highlighted in red.</p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:2; min-width:200px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">DNA Sequence:</label>
    <input id="mn-seq" type="text" value="ACGTACGTAGCTAGCTAG" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; text-transform:uppercase; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <div style="min-width:80px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">k:</label>
    <input id="mn-k" type="number" value="4" min="2" max="8" style="width:70px; padding:6px; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <div style="min-width:80px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">w:</label>
    <input id="mn-w" type="number" value="3" min="2" max="8" style="width:70px; padding:6px; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="mn-run" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer; height:36px;">Compute</button>
</div>
<div id="mn-seq-display" style="font-family:monospace; font-size:1.3em; padding:10px; background:#f5f5f5; border-radius:4px; margin-bottom:10px; letter-spacing:2px; overflow-x:auto; white-space:nowrap;"></div>
<div style="display:flex; gap:8px; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:center;">
  <button id="mn-prev" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#9E9E9E; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Prev Window</button>
  <button id="mn-next" style="padding:6px 14px; background:#4CAF50; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Next Window</button>
  <span id="mn-wininfo" style="font-size:0.9em; margin-left:8px;"></span>
</div>
<div id="mn-table" style="max-height:300px; overflow-y:auto; margin-bottom:10px;"></div>
<div id="mn-stats" style="padding:10px; background:#e8f5e9; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  var $ = function(id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var windows = [];
  var allKmers = [];
  var minimizerPositions = {};
  var currentWin = 0;

  function compute() {
    var seq = $('mn-seq').value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, '');
    var k = parseInt($('mn-k').value);
    var w = parseInt($('mn-w').value);
    if (k < 2 || w < 2 || k + w - 1 > seq.length) {
      $('mn-stats').innerHTML = '<span style="color:#f44336;">Sequence too short for given k and w. Need at least k+w-1 = ' + (k + w - 1) + ' bases.</span>';
      return;
    }

    // Extract all k-mers
    allKmers = [];
    for (var i = 0; i <= seq.length - k; i++) {
      allKmers.push({pos: i, kmer: seq.substring(i, i + k)});
    }

    // Find minimizer for each window of w consecutive k-mers
    windows = [];
    minimizerPositions = {};
    for (var i = 0; i <= allKmers.length - w; i++) {
      var winKmers = allKmers.slice(i, i + w);
      var minIdx = 0;
      for (var j = 1; j < winKmers.length; j++) {
        if (winKmers[j].kmer < winKmers[minIdx].kmer) {
          minIdx = j;
        }
      }
      var minPos = winKmers[minIdx].pos;
      windows.push({start: i, end: i + w - 1, minimizerIdx: minIdx, minimizerPos: minPos, minimizerKmer: winKmers[minIdx].kmer});
      minimizerPositions[minPos] = true;
    }

    currentWin = 0;
    renderAll(seq, k, w);
  }

  function renderAll(seq, k, w) {
    // Sequence display
    var html = '';
    for (var i = 0; i < seq.length; i++) {
      var bg = minimizerPositions[i] !== undefined ? '#e53935' : 'transparent';
      var col = minimizerPositions[i] !== undefined ? 'white' : '#333';
      html += '<span id="mn-c-' + i + '" style="display:inline-block;width:1.2em;text-align:center;padding:2px 0;border-radius:3px;background:' + bg + ';color:' + col + ';">' + seq[i] + '</span>';
    }
    $('mn-seq-display').innerHTML = html;

    // Table of all k-mers with minimizer flags
    var thtml = '<table style="width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:0.85em;">';
    thtml += '<tr style="background:#2196F3;color:white;"><th style="padding:4px 8px;">Pos</th><th style="padding:4px 8px;">K-mer</th><th style="padding:4px 8px;">Minimizer?</th></tr>';
    allKmers.forEach(function(item, i) {
      var isMin = minimizerPositions[item.pos] !== undefined;
      var bg = isMin ? '#ffcdd2' : (i % 2 === 0 ? '#f9f9f9' : '#fff');
      thtml += '<tr id="mn-row-' + i + '" style="background:' + bg + ';">';
      thtml += '<td style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:center;">' + item.pos + '</td>';
      thtml += '<td style="padding:4px 8px;font-family:monospace;">' + item.kmer + '</td>';
      thtml += '<td style="padding:4px 8px;text-align:center;">' + (isMin ? 'Yes' : '') + '</td>';
      thtml += '</tr>';
    });
    thtml += '</table>';
    $('mn-table').innerHTML = thtml;

    // Stats
    var numMinimizers = Object.keys(minimizerPositions).length;
    var totalKmers = allKmers.length;
    var density = (numMinimizers / totalKmers * 100).toFixed(1);
    var theoreticalDensity = (2 / (w + 1) * 100).toFixed(1);
    $('mn-stats').innerHTML = '<strong>Total k-mers:</strong> ' + totalKmers +
      ' | <strong>Windows:</strong> ' + windows.length +
      ' | <strong>Distinct minimizer positions:</strong> ' + numMinimizers +
      ' | <strong>Density:</strong> ' + density + '% (theoretical for random: ~' + theoreticalDensity + '%)';

    highlightWindow(seq, k);
  }

  function highlightWindow(seq, k) {
    // Reset highlights to base state
    for (var i = 0; i < seq.length; i++) {
      var el = document.getElementById('mn-c-' + i);
      if (el) {
        if (minimizerPositions[i] !== undefined) {
          el.style.background = '#e53935';
          el.style.color = 'white';
        } else {
          el.style.background = 'transparent';
          el.style.color = '#333';
        }
        el.style.borderBottom = 'none';
      }
    }
    if (currentWin >= 0 && currentWin < windows.length) {
      var win = windows[currentWin];
      // Highlight window range with underline
      for (var j = allKmers[win.start].pos; j < allKmers[win.end].pos + k; j++) {
        var el2 = document.getElementById('mn-c-' + j);
        if (el2) el2.style.borderBottom = '3px solid #1565C0';
      }
      // Highlight minimizer in this window
      for (var j = win.minimizerPos; j < win.minimizerPos + k; j++) {
        var el3 = document.getElementById('mn-c-' + j);
        if (el3) { el3.style.background = '#1565C0'; el3.style.color = 'white'; }
      }
      $('mn-wininfo').innerHTML = 'Window ' + (currentWin + 1) + '/' + windows.length +
        ': k-mers at positions ' + win.start + '-' + win.end +
        ' | Minimizer: <strong>' + win.minimizerKmer + '</strong> at pos ' + win.minimizerPos;
    }
  }

  $('mn-run').addEventListener('click', compute);
  $('mn-next').addEventListener('click', function() {
    if (currentWin < windows.length - 1) {
      currentWin++;
      highlightWindow($('mn-seq').value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, ''), parseInt($('mn-k').value));
    }
  });
  $('mn-prev').addEventListener('click', function() {
    if (currentWin > 0) {
      currentWin--;
      highlightWindow($('mn-seq').value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, ''), parseInt($('mn-k').value));
    }
  });
  compute();
})();
</script>
```

---

## 6. Minimap2: A Deep Dive

**Minimap2** ([Li, *Bioinformatics* 2018](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/bty191)) is arguably the most versatile sequence alignment tool in genomics today. It handles short reads, long noisy reads (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore with ~15% error), cDNA, and genome-to-genome alignment -- all in a single tool. It is 3-4x faster than BWA-MEM for short reads and 30x or more faster than previous long-read mappers.

The secret to minimap2's speed and versatility is a four-stage pipeline built on minimizers.

### Stage 1: Indexing

Minimap2 builds an index of the reference genome by:

1. Extracting all $(w, k)$-minimizers from the reference
2. Storing them in a hash table: **minimizer $\rightarrow$ list of positions**

| Preset | k | w | Use case |
|--------|---|---|----------|
| `map-ont` | 15 | 10 | Oxford Nanopore reads |
| `map-pb` | 19 | 19 | PacBio CLR reads |
| `sr` | 21 | 11 | Short reads (Illumina) |
| `asm5` | 19 | 19 | Assembly-to-assembly ($<$5% divergence) |

The index for the human genome is typically **~6 GB** in memory -- much smaller than a full k-mer index.

### Stage 2: Seeding (Anchor Finding)

For each query sequence (read):

1. Extract the same $(w, k)$-minimizers from the query
2. Look up each minimizer in the reference index
3. Each match produces an **anchor**: a pair $(x, y)$ where $x$ is the reference position and $y$ is the query position

The result is a set of anchors -- potential match points between query and reference.

### Stage 3: Chaining

Anchors must be grouped into **chains** representing co-linear matches. Minimap2 uses dynamic programming to find the highest-scoring chain:

$$f(i) = \max \left( s_i, \max_{j < i} \left[ f(j) + s_i - \text{gap\_cost}(i, j) \right] \right)$$

where $s_i$ is the seed score and the gap cost penalizes large jumps in either the reference or query coordinate. The gap cost accounts for both distance between anchors and the difference between reference and query gaps (indels).

:::{.callout-note}
## Chaining Complexity
A naive implementation of chaining is $O(n^2)$ in the number of anchors. Minimap2 optimizes this with a band-limited approach -- it only considers anchors within a distance threshold, achieving practical near-linear performance.
:::

### Stage 4: Base-Level Alignment

For each chain, minimap2 performs base-level alignment between the chained anchors. Two key innovations make this practical for long, noisy reads:

**Two-piece affine gap scoring:**

Instead of the standard affine gap penalty $\gamma(l) = o + e \cdot l$ (gap open $o$ + gap extend $e$ times length $l$), minimap2 uses:

$$\gamma(l) = \min(o_1 + e_1 \cdot l, \; o_2 + e_2 \cdot l)$$

where $(o_1, e_1)$ penalizes short gaps with a lower open cost, and $(o_2, e_2)$ penalizes long gaps with a higher open cost but lower extension cost. This two-piece model better handles the mix of short indels (from sequencing errors) and long gaps (from structural variants or introns).

**Z-drop heuristic:**

Minimap2 stops extending an alignment when the score drops by more than $Z$ below the maximum score seen so far:

$$\text{Stop if } \; S_{\max} - S_{\text{current}} > Z$$

This prevents wasting time on poor extensions at the ends of alignments, which is critical for long reads where only a portion may align.

### Minimap2 Versatility

| Mode | What it aligns | Key feature |
|------|---------------|-------------|
| Long reads to reference | ONT/PacBio to genome | Handles 15% error rate |
| Short reads to reference | Illumina to genome | 3-4x faster than BWA-MEM |
| Splice-aware | cDNA/RNA to genome | Finds GT-AG splice sites |
| Assembly to assembly | Contigs to reference | Detects structural variants |

:::{.callout-important}
## Key Insight
Minimap2 demonstrates how minimizers transform sequence alignment. By replacing exact k-mer indexing with minimizer-based seeding, minimap2 achieves massive speedups while maintaining sensitivity. The four-stage pipeline -- **index, seed, chain, align** -- has become the dominant paradigm for modern sequence alignment.
:::

```{=html}

<div id="viz-minimap2" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family: Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Minimap2 Pipeline: Seed-Chain-Align Visualization</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">Step through the four stages of the minimap2 algorithm. See how minimizer seeds become anchors, chains, and alignments.</p>
<div style="display:flex; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div style="flex:2; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Reference:</label>
    <input id="mm-ref" type="text" value="ACGTACGTAGCTAGCTAGCTACGTACGT" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; text-transform:uppercase; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <div style="flex:2; min-width:150px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Query:</label>
    <input id="mm-query" type="text" value="GTAGCTAGCTAG" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; text-transform:uppercase; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <div style="min-width:60px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">k:</label>
    <input id="mm-k" type="number" value="4" min="2" max="6" style="width:60px; padding:6px; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <div style="min-width:60px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">w:</label>
    <input id="mm-w" type="number" value="2" min="1" max="4" style="width:60px; padding:6px; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
</div>
<div style="display:flex; gap:8px; margin-bottom:12px; flex-wrap:wrap;">
  <button id="mm-s1" style="padding:8px 14px; background:#9E9E9E; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">1. Index Reference</button>
  <button id="mm-s2" style="padding:8px 14px; background:#9E9E9E; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">2. Find Seeds</button>
  <button id="mm-s3" style="padding:8px 14px; background:#9E9E9E; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">3. Chain Anchors</button>
  <button id="mm-s4" style="padding:8px 14px; background:#9E9E9E; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">4. Align</button>
  <button id="mm-reset" style="padding:8px 14px; background:#f44336; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer;">Reset</button>
</div>
<div style="position:relative;">
<canvas id="mm-canvas" width="860" height="380" style="width:100%; border:1px solid #eee; border-radius:4px; background:#fafafa; cursor:crosshair;"></canvas>
<div id="mm-tooltip" style="display:none; position:absolute; padding:6px 10px; background:rgba(0,0,0,0.85); color:#fff; font-size:0.8em; font-family:monospace; border-radius:4px; pointer-events:none; white-space:nowrap; z-index:10;"></div>
</div>
<div id="mm-log" style="padding:10px; background:#fff3e0; border-radius:4px; font-size:0.9em; margin-top:10px; min-height:40px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  var $ = function(id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var stage = 0;
  var refMinimizers = [];
  var queryMinimizers = [];
  var anchors = [];
  var chains = [];

  function getMinimizers(seq, k, w) {
    var kmers = [];
    for (var i = 0; i <= seq.length - k; i++) {
      kmers.push({pos: i, kmer: seq.substring(i, i + k)});
    }
    var selected = {};
    for (var i = 0; i <= kmers.length - w; i++) {
      var minIdx = i;
      for (var j = i + 1; j < i + w; j++) {
        if (kmers[j].kmer < kmers[minIdx].kmer) minIdx = j;
      }
      selected[minIdx] = kmers[minIdx];
    }
    var result = [];
    Object.keys(selected).forEach(function(idx) { result.push(selected[idx]); });
    result.sort(function(a, b) { return a.pos - b.pos; });
    return result;
  }

  function findAnchors(refMins, queryMins) {
    var anch = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < queryMins.length; i++) {
      for (var j = 0; j < refMins.length; j++) {
        if (queryMins[i].kmer === refMins[j].kmer) {
          anch.push({rx: refMins[j].pos, qy: queryMins[i].pos, kmer: queryMins[i].kmer});
        }
      }
    }
    return anch;
  }

  function chainAnchors(anch) {
    if (anch.length === 0) return [];
    // Simplified greedy chaining shown here; minimap2 uses dynamic programming with gap penalties
    var sorted = anch.slice().sort(function(a, b) { return a.rx - b.rx || a.qy - b.qy; });
    var bestChain = [sorted[0]];
    for (var i = 1; i < sorted.length; i++) {
      var prev = bestChain[bestChain.length - 1];
      if (sorted[i].rx > prev.rx && sorted[i].qy > prev.qy) {
        bestChain.push(sorted[i]);
      }
    }
    return bestChain;
  }

  function draw() {
    var canvas = $('mm-canvas');
    var ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
    var W = canvas.width;
    var H = canvas.height;
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);

    var ref = $('mm-ref').value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, '');
    var query = $('mm-query').value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, '');
    var k = parseInt($('mm-k').value);

    var marginL = 80, marginR = 30, marginT = 50, marginB = 80;
    var plotW = W - marginL - marginR;
    var plotH = H - marginT - marginB;

    // Draw axes
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#333';
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.5;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(marginL, marginT);
    ctx.lineTo(marginL, marginT + plotH);
    ctx.lineTo(marginL + plotW, marginT + plotH);
    ctx.stroke();

    // Axis labels
    ctx.fillStyle = '#333';
    ctx.font = '12px Arial';
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    ctx.fillText('Reference position', marginL + plotW / 2, H - 10);
    ctx.save();
    ctx.translate(18, marginT + plotH / 2);
    ctx.rotate(-Math.PI / 2);
    ctx.fillText('Query position', 0, 0);
    ctx.restore();

    // Draw reference sequence along x-axis
    ctx.font = '10px monospace';
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    var refScale = plotW / Math.max(ref.length, 1);
    for (var i = 0; i < ref.length; i++) {
      ctx.fillStyle = '#666';
      ctx.fillText(ref[i], marginL + i * refScale + refScale / 2, H - 40);
    }

    // Draw query sequence along y-axis
    var queryScale = plotH / Math.max(query.length, 1);
    for (var i = 0; i < query.length; i++) {
      ctx.fillStyle = '#666';
      ctx.textAlign = 'right';
      ctx.fillText(query[i], marginL - 10, marginT + plotH - i * queryScale - queryScale / 2 + 4);
    }

    // Title
    ctx.fillStyle = '#333';
    ctx.font = 'bold 14px Arial';
    ctx.textAlign = 'center';
    var titles = ['Dot Plot View', 'Stage 1: Index Reference Minimizers', 'Stage 2: Find Seed Anchors', 'Stage 3: Chain Co-linear Anchors', 'Stage 4: Base-Level Alignment'];
    ctx.fillText(titles[stage], W / 2, 25);

    if (stage === 0) return;

    // Stage 1+: show reference minimizer positions on x-axis
    if (stage >= 1) {
      refMinimizers.forEach(function(m) {
        var x = marginL + m.pos * refScale + refScale / 2;
        ctx.fillStyle = '#e53935';
        ctx.beginPath();
        ctx.arc(x, marginT + plotH + 12, 4, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
        ctx.fill();
      });
    }

    // Stage 2+: show anchors as dots
    if (stage >= 2) {
      anchors.forEach(function(a) {
        var x = marginL + a.rx * refScale + refScale / 2;
        var y = marginT + plotH - a.qy * queryScale - queryScale / 2;
        ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(33, 150, 243, 0.6)';
        ctx.beginPath();
        ctx.arc(x, y, 5, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
        ctx.fill();
        ctx.strokeStyle = '#1565C0';
        ctx.lineWidth = 1;
        ctx.stroke();
      });
    }

    // Stage 3+: draw chain lines
    if (stage >= 3 && chains.length > 1) {
      ctx.strokeStyle = '#4CAF50';
      ctx.lineWidth = 2.5;
      ctx.setLineDash([]);
      ctx.beginPath();
      for (var i = 0; i < chains.length; i++) {
        var x = marginL + chains[i].rx * refScale + refScale / 2;
        var y = marginT + plotH - chains[i].qy * queryScale - queryScale / 2;
        if (i === 0) ctx.moveTo(x, y); else ctx.lineTo(x, y);
      }
      ctx.stroke();

      // Highlight chain anchors
      chains.forEach(function(a) {
        var x = marginL + a.rx * refScale + refScale / 2;
        var y = marginT + plotH - a.qy * queryScale - queryScale / 2;
        ctx.fillStyle = '#4CAF50';
        ctx.beginPath();
        ctx.arc(x, y, 6, 0, 2 * Math.PI);
        ctx.fill();
      });
    }

    // Stage 4: draw alignment band
    if (stage >= 4 && chains.length > 1) {
      var first = chains[0];
      var last = chains[chains.length - 1];
      var x1 = marginL + first.rx * refScale + refScale / 2;
      var y1 = marginT + plotH - first.qy * queryScale - queryScale / 2;
      var x2 = marginL + (last.rx + k) * refScale;
      var y2 = marginT + plotH - (last.qy + k) * queryScale;
      ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(76, 175, 80, 0.15)';
      ctx.strokeStyle = '#4CAF50';
      ctx.lineWidth = 1;
      ctx.setLineDash([4, 4]);
      var bandW = 15;
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(x1 - bandW, y1 + bandW);
      ctx.lineTo(x2 - bandW, y2 + bandW);
      ctx.lineTo(x2 + bandW, y2 - bandW);
      ctx.lineTo(x1 + bandW, y1 - bandW);
      ctx.closePath();
      ctx.fill();
      ctx.stroke();
      ctx.setLineDash([]);
    }
  }

  function runStage(s) {
    var ref = $('mm-ref').value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, '');
    var query = $('mm-query').value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, '');
    var k = parseInt($('mm-k').value);
    var w = parseInt($('mm-w').value);

    stage = s;
    var log = '';

    if (s >= 1) {
      refMinimizers = getMinimizers(ref, k, w);
      queryMinimizers = getMinimizers(query, k, w);
      log += '<strong>Stage 1 - Index:</strong> Found ' + refMinimizers.length + ' minimizers in reference, ' + queryMinimizers.length + ' in query.<br/>';
      $('mm-s1').style.background = '#2196F3';
    }
    if (s >= 2) {
      anchors = findAnchors(refMinimizers, queryMinimizers);
      log += '<strong>Stage 2 - Seed:</strong> Found ' + anchors.length + ' anchor(s) from shared minimizers.<br/>';
      $('mm-s2').style.background = '#2196F3';
    }
    if (s >= 3) {
      chains = chainAnchors(anchors);
      log += '<strong>Stage 3 - Chain:</strong> Best chain has ' + chains.length + ' co-linear anchor(s).<br/>';
      $('mm-s3').style.background = '#4CAF50';
    }
    if (s >= 4) {
      if (chains.length > 0) {
        var rStart = chains[0].rx;
        var rEnd = chains[chains.length - 1].rx + k;
        var qStart = chains[0].qy;
        var qEnd = chains[chains.length - 1].qy + k;
        log += '<strong>Stage 4 - Align:</strong> Base-level alignment in region ref[' + rStart + '..' + rEnd + '] vs query[' + qStart + '..' + qEnd + '] using two-piece affine gap + Z-drop.<br/>';
      } else {
        log += '<strong>Stage 4:</strong> No chain to align.<br/>';
      }
      $('mm-s4').style.background = '#4CAF50';
    }

    $('mm-log').innerHTML = log;
    draw();
  }

  function resetAll() {
    stage = 0;
    refMinimizers = [];
    queryMinimizers = [];
    anchors = [];
    chains = [];
    ['mm-s1', 'mm-s2', 'mm-s3', 'mm-s4'].forEach(function(id) { $(id).style.background = '#9E9E9E'; });
    $('mm-log').innerHTML = 'Click the stage buttons in order to step through the minimap2 pipeline.';
    draw();
  }

  $('mm-s1').addEventListener('click', function() { runStage(1); });
  $('mm-s2').addEventListener('click', function() { runStage(2); });
  $('mm-s3').addEventListener('click', function() { runStage(3); });
  $('mm-s4').addEventListener('click', function() { runStage(4); });
  $('mm-reset').addEventListener('click', resetAll);

  // Tooltip on hover over anchors/chain points
  $('mm-canvas').addEventListener('mousemove', function(e) {
    var canvas = $('mm-canvas');
    var rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
    var scaleX = canvas.width / rect.width;
    var scaleY = canvas.height / rect.height;
    var mx = (e.clientX - rect.left) * scaleX;
    var my = (e.clientY - rect.top) * scaleY;

    var ref = $('mm-ref').value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, '');
    var query = $('mm-query').value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, '');
    var k = parseInt($('mm-k').value);
    var marginL = 80, marginR = 30, marginT = 50, marginB = 80;
    var plotW = canvas.width - marginL - marginR;
    var plotH = canvas.height - marginT - marginB;
    var refScale = plotW / Math.max(ref.length, 1);
    var queryScale = plotH / Math.max(query.length, 1);

    var tooltip = $('mm-tooltip');
    var hit = null;
    var hitDist = 12; // pixel threshold

    // Check anchors (stage 2+) and chain points (stage 3+)
    var pts = stage >= 3 ? chains : (stage >= 2 ? anchors : []);
    for (var i = 0; i < pts.length; i++) {
      var px = marginL + pts[i].rx * refScale + refScale / 2;
      var py = marginT + plotH - pts[i].qy * queryScale - queryScale / 2;
      var d = Math.sqrt((mx - px) * (mx - px) + (my - py) * (my - py));
      if (d < hitDist) {
        hit = pts[i];
        hitDist = d;
      }
    }
    // Also check non-chain anchors if in stage 3+
    if (stage >= 3) {
      for (var i = 0; i < anchors.length; i++) {
        var px = marginL + anchors[i].rx * refScale + refScale / 2;
        var py = marginT + plotH - anchors[i].qy * queryScale - queryScale / 2;
        var d = Math.sqrt((mx - px) * (mx - px) + (my - py) * (my - py));
        if (d < hitDist) {
          hit = anchors[i];
          hitDist = d;
        }
      }
    }

    if (hit) {
      var inChain = false;
      if (stage >= 3) {
        for (var i = 0; i < chains.length; i++) {
          if (chains[i].rx === hit.rx && chains[i].qy === hit.qy) { inChain = true; break; }
        }
      }
      var label = 'k-mer: ' + hit.kmer + '  ref: ' + hit.rx + '  query: ' + hit.qy;
      if (stage >= 3) label += inChain ? '  [chained]' : '  [unchained]';
      tooltip.textContent = label;
      tooltip.style.display = 'block';
      // Position relative to container, accounting for canvas scaling
      tooltip.style.left = (e.clientX - rect.left + 12) + 'px';
      tooltip.style.top = (e.clientY - rect.top - 28) + 'px';
    } else {
      tooltip.style.display = 'none';
    }
  });

  $('mm-canvas').addEventListener('mouseleave', function() {
    $('mm-tooltip').style.display = 'none';
  });

  resetAll();
})();
</script>
```

---

## 7. Mash: Fast Genome Distance Estimation

### The Problem: Comparing Thousands of Genomes

Imagine you have 54,118 genomes from NCBI RefSeq and want to know which are closely related. Pairwise whole-genome alignment would require over **1.4 billion** comparisons, each taking minutes to hours. Even with fast aligners, this is computationally prohibitive.

What if we could estimate genome similarity in **microseconds** per pair -- without performing any alignment at all?

### Genomes as K-mer Sets

We already know how to decompose a sequence into k-mers. A key insight is that we can treat an entire genome as a **set** of its constituent k-mers:

- Two identical genomes share **all** k-mers
- A single mutation destroys $k$ overlapping k-mers
- Unrelated genomes share almost **no** k-mers (for sufficiently large $k$)

This transforms a sequence comparison problem into a **set comparison** problem. And set comparison has well-studied, efficient solutions.

### Jaccard Index: Measuring Set Similarity

The **Jaccard index** measures the overlap between two sets:

$$J(A, B) = \frac{|A \cap B|}{|A \cup B|}$$

Where $A$ and $B$ are the k-mer sets of two genomes:

- **Numerator** $|A \cap B|$ (intersection): the number of k-mers that appear in **both** genomes -- the shared k-mers.
- **Denominator** $|A \cup B|$ (union): the number of **distinct** k-mers that appear in **either** genome (or both), counting each unique k-mer only once.

For example, if genome A has k-mers {`ACG`, `CGT`, `GTA`, `TAC`} and genome B has {`ACG`, `CGT`, `GTG`, `TGA`}:

| | K-mers | Size |
|---|---|---|
| $A \cap B$ (shared) | `ACG`, `CGT` | 2 |
| $A \cup B$ (all unique) | `ACG`, `CGT`, `GTA`, `TAC`, `GTG`, `TGA` | 6 |

$$J = \frac{2}{6} = 0.333$$

Dividing by the union rather than the size of one set ensures the measure is symmetric ($J(A,B) = J(B,A)$) and bounded between 0 and 1:

- $J = 1$: the sets are identical
- $J = 0$: the sets share no elements
- $J \approx 0.5$: about half the elements are shared

For two genomes represented as k-mer sets, the Jaccard index captures their overall similarity. If two genomes are 95% identical, their k-mer sets overlap a lot, giving a high Jaccard. If they are distantly related, the Jaccard drops near zero. The problem? A single bacterial genome produces **millions** of k-mers. Comparing every k-mer between two whole genomes is prohibitively expensive.

### K-mer Sketches

A **sketch** is a small, fixed-size summary of a sequence's k-mer content that lets you estimate similarity without comparing full k-mer sets. Instead of storing hundreds of millions of k-mers, a sketch compresses them down to, say, 1000 representative values -- and you compare those instead.

:::{.callout-tip}
## Quick Intuition
Think of a sketch like a fingerprint. You don't need to compare every ridge of two fingerprints to know they match -- a small set of distinctive features is enough. Sketches do the same for genomes: they capture just enough of the k-mer landscape to reliably estimate how similar two sequences are, at a tiny fraction of the cost.
:::

### MinHash Sketching

The most common sketching approach is **MinHash** (Broder, 1997). The idea:

1. **Hash** every k-mer in the sequence to a number
2. **Keep** only the $s$ smallest hash values (the "bottom-$s$ sketch")
3. **Compare** sketches instead of full sets

```
All k-mers:   hash → [0.72, 0.11, 0.95, 0.03, 0.44, 0.67, 0.28, ...]
                                          ↓
Keep bottom s=3:      [0.03, 0.11, 0.28]   ← this is your sketch
```

To estimate the Jaccard index between two sequences, count how many of the smallest hashes they share:

```
Sketch A: [0.03, 0.11, 0.28]
Sketch B: [0.03, 0.14, 0.28]

Shared: 0.03 and 0.28  →  J ≈ 2/4 = 0.5
```

The fraction of shared elements between two sketches **approximates** the Jaccard index:

$$J(A, B) \approx \frac{|\text{sketch}(A) \cap \text{sketch}(B)|}{|\text{sketch}(A) \cup \text{sketch}(B)|}$$

Why does this work? A random hash function maps set elements uniformly across the hash space. The probability that the minimum hash value comes from the intersection $A \cap B$ equals $\frac{|A \cap B|}{|A \cup B|}$ -- exactly the Jaccard index. Keeping the bottom-$s$ values rather than just the minimum gives us $s$ independent estimates, improving accuracy.

With a sketch size of $s = 1000$, each genome is reduced to a fingerprint of just **a few kilobytes** -- regardless of whether the genome is 5 million or 3 billion bases long.

### Connection to Minimizers

A minimizer is essentially MinHash applied to a **local window**. The key differences:

| | MinHash Sketch | Minimizers |
|---|---|---|
| **Scope** | Whole sequence | Local window |
| **Purpose** | Global similarity | Local alignment anchors |
| **Output** | A set of $s$ hash values | A representative k-mer per window |

Both techniques rely on the same core insight -- select a small number of representative k-mers using hash values -- but they serve different goals. Minimizers find local anchors for alignment; MinHash sketches estimate global similarity.

### What You Can Estimate From a Sketch

Sketches enable several types of queries:

- **Jaccard similarity** -- are these sequences similar?
- **Containment** -- is genome A contained within genome B? (useful for metagenomics)
- **Genome distance** -- Mash converts Jaccard to an evolutionary distance (see next section)

### Tools Built on Sketching

| Tool | Sketch Type | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| **Mash** | MinHash (bottom-$s$) | Genome distance, contamination detection |
| **Sourmash** | FracMinHash (scaled) | Metagenome classification, containment |
| **Dashing** | HyperLogLog | Ultra-fast cardinality and similarity |
| **HULK** | Histogram sketching | Streaming metagenomics |

### From Jaccard to Mash Distance

The Jaccard index measures k-mer set overlap, but biologists think in terms of mutation rates. Mash (Ondov et al., 2016) converts the Jaccard index to a **Mash distance** $D$ that approximates the average nucleotide identity (ANI):

$$D = \frac{-1}{k} \ln \frac{2J}{1+J}$$

The intuition: a single nucleotide mutation destroys $k$ overlapping k-mers, so the relationship between mutation rate and k-mer similarity depends on $k$. The formula accounts for this by scaling by $\frac{1}{k}$.

| Mash Distance $D$ | Approximate ANI | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0 | 100% | Identical genomes |
| 0.005 | 99.5% | Same species (strains) |
| 0.05 | ~95% | Species boundary |
| 0.3+ | <70% | Different genera/families |

:::{.callout-note}
## ANI and the Species Boundary
An ANI of ~95% is widely used as a species delineation threshold for prokaryotes. Mash distances below ~0.05 reliably identify members of the same species, making Mash a practical tool for taxonomic classification.
:::

### The Mash Pipeline

The complete Mash pipeline has just three steps:

1. **K-merize** each genome (default $k = 21$)
2. **Hash and sketch**: apply a hash function, keep the bottom-$s$ values (default $s = 1000$)
3. **Compare sketches**: count shared hashes between any two sketches in $O(s)$ time

The critical insight: **sketch size is independent of genome size**. Comparing two sketches of size 1000 takes the same time whether the genomes are 5 Mb bacteria or 3 Gb mammals. This makes all-vs-all comparison feasible: 54,118 genomes were clustered in just **33 CPU-hours** by Ondov et al. (2016).

### Interactive Mash Demo

```{=html}
<div id="viz-mash" style="max-width:900px; margin:2em auto; font-family:Arial, sans-serif;">
<h4 style="text-align:center; color:#333;">Interactive MinHash Sketch & Mash Distance Demo</h4>
<p style="text-align:center; color:#666; font-size:0.9em;">Enter two DNA sequences to see how MinHash sketches approximate the Jaccard index and compute Mash distance.</p>

<div style="display:flex; gap:16px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:12px;">
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:250px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Sequence A:</label>
    <input id="mash-seqA" type="text" value="ACGTACGTAGCTAGCTAGCATGCATGCA" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; text-transform:uppercase; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
  <div style="flex:1; min-width:250px;">
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Sequence B:</label>
    <input id="mash-seqB" type="text" value="ACGTACGTAGCTAGCTTTTCATGCATGCA" style="width:100%; padding:6px; font-family:monospace; text-transform:uppercase; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px;" />
  </div>
</div>
<div style="display:flex; gap:16px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:12px; align-items:flex-end;">
  <div>
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">k: <span id="mash-k-val">5</span></label>
    <input id="mash-k" type="range" min="3" max="9" value="5" style="width:100px;" />
  </div>
  <div>
    <label style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold;">Sketch size (s): <span id="mash-s-val">6</span></label>
    <input id="mash-s" type="range" min="2" max="20" value="6" style="width:120px;" />
  </div>
  <button id="mash-run" style="padding:8px 16px; background:#2196F3; color:white; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer; height:36px;">Compute</button>
</div>

<div id="mash-output" style="margin-top:10px;"></div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  function $(id) { return document.getElementById(id); }

  function simpleHash(str) {
    // Simple but deterministic hash for demo purposes
    var hash = 0;
    for (var i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
      hash = ((hash << 5) - hash + str.charCodeAt(i)) | 0;
    }
    return hash >>> 0; // Convert to unsigned 32-bit
  }

  function getKmers(seq, k) {
    var kmers = [];
    seq = seq.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, '');
    for (var i = 0; i <= seq.length - k; i++) {
      kmers.push(seq.substring(i, i + k));
    }
    return kmers;
  }

  function uniqueArray(arr) {
    var seen = {};
    return arr.filter(function(item) {
      if (seen[item]) return false;
      seen[item] = true;
      return true;
    });
  }

  function computeMash() {
    var seqA = $('mash-seqA').value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, '');
    var seqB = $('mash-seqB').value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^ACGT]/g, '');
    var k = parseInt($('mash-k').value);
    var s = parseInt($('mash-s').value);
    $('mash-k-val').textContent = k;
    $('mash-s-val').textContent = s;

    if (seqA.length < k || seqB.length < k) {
      $('mash-output').innerHTML = '<p style="color:#c00;">Sequences must be at least k=' + k + ' characters long.</p>';
      return;
    }

    // Step 1: Extract k-mers
    var kmersA = uniqueArray(getKmers(seqA, k));
    var kmersB = uniqueArray(getKmers(seqB, k));

    // Step 2: Hash all k-mers
    var hashesA = kmersA.map(function(km) { return { kmer: km, hash: simpleHash(km) }; });
    var hashesB = kmersB.map(function(km) { return { kmer: km, hash: simpleHash(km) }; });

    // Sort by hash value
    hashesA.sort(function(a, b) { return a.hash - b.hash; });
    hashesB.sort(function(a, b) { return a.hash - b.hash; });

    // Step 3: Select bottom-s sketch
    var sketchA = hashesA.slice(0, s);
    var sketchB = hashesB.slice(0, s);

    // Step 4: Compute exact Jaccard
    var setA = {};
    var setB = {};
    kmersA.forEach(function(km) { setA[km] = true; });
    kmersB.forEach(function(km) { setB[km] = true; });
    var intersection = 0;
    var union = {};
    kmersA.forEach(function(km) { union[km] = true; });
    kmersB.forEach(function(km) { union[km] = true; });
    kmersA.forEach(function(km) { if (setB[km]) intersection++; });
    var exactJ = intersection / Object.keys(union).length;

    // Step 5: Compute sketch-based Jaccard
    var sketchHashSetA = {};
    var sketchHashSetB = {};
    sketchA.forEach(function(h) { sketchHashSetA[h.hash] = h.kmer; });
    sketchB.forEach(function(h) { sketchHashSetB[h.hash] = h.kmer; });
    // Merge sketches, take bottom-s of combined, count shared
    var combined = {};
    sketchA.forEach(function(h) { combined[h.hash] = { a: true, kmer: h.kmer }; });
    sketchB.forEach(function(h) {
      if (combined[h.hash]) { combined[h.hash].b = true; }
      else { combined[h.hash] = { b: true, kmer: h.kmer }; }
    });
    var allHashes = Object.keys(combined).map(Number).sort(function(a, b) { return a - b; });
    var bottomS = allHashes.slice(0, s);
    var shared = 0;
    bottomS.forEach(function(h) {
      if (combined[h].a && combined[h].b) shared++;
    });
    var sketchJ = shared / bottomS.length;

    // Step 6: Mash distance
    function mashDist(j) {
      if (j === 0) return Infinity;
      var inner = (2 * j) / (1 + j);
      if (inner <= 0) return Infinity;
      return (-1 / k) * Math.log(inner);
    }
    var exactD = mashDist(exactJ);
    var sketchD = mashDist(sketchJ);

    // Build display
    var html = '';

    // K-mer extraction summary
    html += '<div style="display:flex; gap:16px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:12px;">';
    html += '<div style="flex:1; min-width:200px; background:#f0f7ff; padding:10px; border-radius:6px; border:1px solid #c0d8f0;">';
    html += '<strong>Sequence A:</strong> ' + kmersA.length + ' distinct k-mers</div>';
    html += '<div style="flex:1; min-width:200px; background:#f0fff0; padding:10px; border-radius:6px; border:1px solid #c0e0c0;">';
    html += '<strong>Sequence B:</strong> ' + kmersB.length + ' distinct k-mers</div>';
    html += '</div>';

    // --- Panel 1: Exact Jaccard (all k-mers) ---
    html += '<div style="background:#faf0ff; padding:14px; border-radius:6px; border:1px solid #d0b8e0; margin-bottom:12px;">';
    html += '<h5 style="margin:0 0 8px 0; color:#6A1B9A;">Exact Jaccard (all k-mers, no sketching)</h5>';
    html += '<div style="display:flex; gap:16px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px;">';

    // All k-mers column A
    html += '<div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">';
    html += '<div style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold; margin-bottom:4px; color:#1565C0;">A\'s k-mers (' + kmersA.length + ')</div>';
    html += '<div style="max-height:180px; overflow-y:auto; border:1px solid #ddd; border-radius:4px;">';
    html += '<table style="width:100%; font-size:0.82em; border-collapse:collapse;">';
    kmersA.forEach(function(km) {
      var isShared = setB[km];
      var bg = isShared ? '#e1bee7' : '#fff';
      html += '<tr style="background:' + bg + ';"><td style="padding:2px 6px; font-family:monospace;">' + km + '</td>';
      html += '<td style="padding:2px 6px; text-align:center; font-size:0.9em;">' + (isShared ? 'shared' : '') + '</td></tr>';
    });
    html += '</table></div></div>';

    // All k-mers column B
    html += '<div style="flex:1; min-width:150px;">';
    html += '<div style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold; margin-bottom:4px; color:#2E7D32;">B\'s k-mers (' + kmersB.length + ')</div>';
    html += '<div style="max-height:180px; overflow-y:auto; border:1px solid #ddd; border-radius:4px;">';
    html += '<table style="width:100%; font-size:0.82em; border-collapse:collapse;">';
    kmersB.forEach(function(km) {
      var isShared = setA[km];
      var bg = isShared ? '#e1bee7' : '#fff';
      html += '<tr style="background:' + bg + ';"><td style="padding:2px 6px; font-family:monospace;">' + km + '</td>';
      html += '<td style="padding:2px 6px; text-align:center; font-size:0.9em;">' + (isShared ? 'shared' : '') + '</td></tr>';
    });
    html += '</table></div></div>';

    // Exact results
    html += '<div style="flex:1; min-width:160px; background:#f3e5f5; padding:10px; border-radius:6px; align-self:flex-start;">';
    html += '<div style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold; margin-bottom:6px;">Exact Result</div>';
    html += '<div>|A &cap; B|: <strong>' + intersection + '</strong></div>';
    html += '<div>|A &cup; B|: <strong>' + Object.keys(union).length + '</strong></div>';
    html += '<div style="margin-top:6px; font-size:1.1em;">J = ' + intersection + '/' + Object.keys(union).length + ' = <strong>' + exactJ.toFixed(4) + '</strong></div>';
    html += '<div style="margin-top:4px;">Mash D = <strong>' + (isFinite(exactD) ? exactD.toFixed(4) : 'undef (J=0)') + '</strong></div>';
    html += '</div>';
    html += '</div></div>';

    // --- Panel 2: Sketch-based estimate ---
    html += '<div style="background:#f0f7ff; padding:14px; border-radius:6px; border:1px solid #b0cfe0; margin-bottom:12px;">';
    html += '<h5 style="margin:0 0 8px 0; color:#1565C0;">Sketch Estimate (MinHash, s=' + s + ')</h5>';
    html += '<div style="display:flex; gap:16px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-bottom:10px;">';

    // Sketch column A
    html += '<div style="flex:1; min-width:200px;">';
    html += '<div style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold; margin-bottom:4px; color:#1565C0;">Sketch A (bottom-' + Math.min(s, hashesA.length) + ' hashes)</div>';
    html += '<div style="max-height:220px; overflow-y:auto; border:1px solid #ddd; border-radius:4px;">';
    html += '<table style="width:100%; font-size:0.82em; border-collapse:collapse;">';
    html += '<tr style="background:#e3f2fd;"><th style="padding:3px 6px; text-align:left;">K-mer</th><th style="padding:3px 6px; text-align:right;">Hash</th><th style="padding:3px 6px;">In sketch?</th></tr>';
    hashesA.forEach(function(h, i) {
      var inSketch = i < s;
      var isShared = inSketch && sketchHashSetB[h.hash] !== undefined;
      var bg = isShared ? '#fff9c4' : (inSketch ? '#e8f5e9' : '#fff');
      html += '<tr style="background:' + bg + ';">';
      html += '<td style="padding:2px 6px; font-family:monospace;">' + h.kmer + '</td>';
      html += '<td style="padding:2px 6px; text-align:right; font-family:monospace;">' + h.hash + '</td>';
      html += '<td style="padding:2px 6px; text-align:center;">' + (inSketch ? (isShared ? '&#x2713; shared' : '&#x2713;') : '') + '</td>';
      html += '</tr>';
    });
    html += '</table></div></div>';

    // Sketch column B
    html += '<div style="flex:1; min-width:200px;">';
    html += '<div style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold; margin-bottom:4px; color:#2E7D32;">Sketch B (bottom-' + Math.min(s, hashesB.length) + ' hashes)</div>';
    html += '<div style="max-height:220px; overflow-y:auto; border:1px solid #ddd; border-radius:4px;">';
    html += '<table style="width:100%; font-size:0.82em; border-collapse:collapse;">';
    html += '<tr style="background:#e8f5e9;"><th style="padding:3px 6px; text-align:left;">K-mer</th><th style="padding:3px 6px; text-align:right;">Hash</th><th style="padding:3px 6px;">In sketch?</th></tr>';
    hashesB.forEach(function(h, i) {
      var inSketch = i < s;
      var isShared = inSketch && sketchHashSetA[h.hash] !== undefined;
      var bg = isShared ? '#fff9c4' : (inSketch ? '#e8f5e9' : '#fff');
      html += '<tr style="background:' + bg + ';">';
      html += '<td style="padding:2px 6px; font-family:monospace;">' + h.kmer + '</td>';
      html += '<td style="padding:2px 6px; text-align:right; font-family:monospace;">' + h.hash + '</td>';
      html += '<td style="padding:2px 6px; text-align:center;">' + (inSketch ? (isShared ? '&#x2713; shared' : '&#x2713;') : '') + '</td>';
      html += '</tr>';
    });
    html += '</table></div></div>';
    html += '</div>';

    // Sketch results
    html += '<div style="background:#e3f2fd; padding:10px; border-radius:6px;">';
    html += '<div style="display:flex; gap:20px; flex-wrap:wrap; align-items:flex-start;">';
    html += '<div style="flex:1; min-width:160px;">';
    html += '<div style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold; margin-bottom:4px;">Sketch Result</div>';
    html += '<div>Shared in bottom-' + bottomS.length + ': <strong>' + shared + '</strong></div>';
    html += '<div style="font-size:1.1em;">Sketch J = <strong>' + sketchJ.toFixed(4) + '</strong></div>';
    html += '<div>Sketch Mash D = <strong>' + (isFinite(sketchD) ? sketchD.toFixed(4) : 'undef (J=0)') + '</strong></div>';
    html += '</div>';
    html += '<div style="flex:1; min-width:160px; background:#fff3e0; padding:8px; border-radius:6px; border:1px solid #ffe0b2;">';
    html += '<div style="font-size:0.85em; font-weight:bold; margin-bottom:4px;">Sketch vs Exact</div>';
    html += '<div>Jaccard error: <strong>' + Math.abs(exactJ - sketchJ).toFixed(4) + '</strong></div>';
    html += '<div>Mash D error: <strong>' + (isFinite(exactD) && isFinite(sketchD) ? Math.abs(exactD - sketchD).toFixed(4) : 'N/A') + '</strong></div>';
    html += '<div style="margin-top:4px; font-size:0.82em; color:#666;">Increase s to reduce error</div>';
    html += '</div>';
    html += '</div></div>';
    html += '</div>';

    $('mash-output').innerHTML = html;
  }

  $('mash-run').addEventListener('click', computeMash);
  $('mash-k').addEventListener('input', function() { $('mash-k-val').textContent = this.value; });
  $('mash-s').addEventListener('input', function() { $('mash-s-val').textContent = this.value; });

  // Run on load
  computeMash();
})();
</script>
```

:::{.callout-tip}
## Try It
1. Start with the default sequences that differ in the middle. Compare the exact Jaccard (purple panel) with the sketch estimate (blue panel) -- notice the error in "Sketch vs Exact."
2. Make Sequence B identical to Sequence A -- both Jaccard values should become 1.0 and the error should drop to 0.
3. Increase $k$ -- what happens to the Jaccard index when sequences differ?
4. Increase sketch size $s$ -- the sketch estimate becomes more accurate (error shrinks toward zero).
5. Try completely different sequences -- the Jaccard drops near 0 and Mash distance becomes large.
:::

### Sourmash and Scaled MinHash

The standard MinHash sketch keeps exactly $s$ hashes. An alternative approach, **FracMinHash** (also called "scaled MinHash"), keeps all hash values below a threshold $\frac{H}{f}$ where $H$ is the maximum hash value and $f$ is a scaling factor (Brown and Irber, 2016). This means sketch size scales proportionally with genome size, which enables **containment** queries: "what fraction of genome A's k-mers appear in genome B?" This is particularly valuable for metagenomics, where you want to detect the presence of a small genome within a large mixed sample. The tool [sourmash](https://sourmash.readthedocs.io/) implements FracMinHash and has become widely used for metagenomic analysis.

### References

- Ondov BD, Treangen TJ, Melsted P, et al. "Mash: fast genome and metagenome distance estimation using MinHash." *Genome Biology* 17:132, 2016. [DOI: 10.1186/s13059-016-0997-x](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-0997-x)
- Broder AZ. "On the resemblance and containment of documents." *Proceedings of the Compression and Complexity of Sequences*, 21-29, 1997.
- Brown CT, Irber L. "sourmash: a library for MinHash sketching of DNA." *JOSS* 1(5):27, 2016.

---

## 8. Summary

This lecture traced the journey from k-mers to modern sequence analysis:

| Concept | Key Idea | Tools |
|---------|----------|-------|
| **K-mers** | Sliding window of length k over a sequence; $4^k$ possible | Foundation of all methods |
| **K-mer counting** | Hash tables and disk-based sorting to tally k-mers | Jellyfish, KMC 2/3 |
| **K-mer frequency histogram** | Count distribution reveals genome properties | GenomeScope, Merqury |
| **Minimizers** | Smallest k-mer in a window; reduces index by ~80% | [Roberts et al. 2004](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/bth408) |
| **Minimap2** | Index-seed-chain-align pipeline using minimizers | [Li 2018](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/bty191) |
| **Mash** | MinHash sketches for fast genome distance estimation | [Ondov et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-0997-x) |

The thread connecting everything: **k-mers are the atomic unit of sequence analysis**. We count them to profile genomes. We subsample them with minimizers to build efficient indexes. We chain minimizer hits to find alignments. And we use k-mer set operations to evaluate assemblies.

:::{.callout-important}
## The Big Picture
The progression in this lecture mirrors a recurring theme in computational genomics: **start with a brute-force approach, understand its limitations, then find a clever subsampling or indexing strategy that preserves the essential information while dramatically reducing computational cost**. K-mers to minimizers is one of the clearest examples of this pattern.
:::

### Looking Ahead

K-mers and minimizers appear throughout modern genomics:

- **Genome assembly**: De Bruijn graphs are built from k-mers (SPAdes, hifiasm). Efficient construction of compacted de Bruijn graphs has been advanced by algorithms like **TwoPaCo** ([Minkin et al., *Bioinformatics* 2017](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btw609)) and **BCALM 2** ([Chikhi, Limasset, and Medvedev, *Bioinformatics* 2016](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btw279)), which use minimizer-based partitioning for scalable graph construction.
- **Metagenomic classification**: [Kraken 2](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-019-1891-0) maps minimizers to taxonomic labels (building on the original [Kraken](https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46) by [Wood and Salzberg, *Genome Biology* 2014](https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2014-15-3-r46))
- **Sequence comparison**: Mash and sourmash (covered in Section 7) extend to metagenomics, environmental sampling, and outbreak tracking
- **Error correction**: Tools like BFC correct reads based on k-mer frequencies
- **K-mer set representations**: [Rahman and Medvedev (*RECOMB* 2020)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-45257-5_10) introduced **spectrum-preserving string sets (SPSS)**, a compact way to represent a set of k-mers as a collection of strings that preserves all k-mer membership and abundance information. Their UST algorithm finds a near-optimal SPSS by computing a path cover of the compacted de Bruijn graph.
- **K-mer data structure surveys**: A comprehensive review by [Marchet, Boucher, Puglisi, Medvedev, Salson, and Chikhi (*Genome Research* 2021)](https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.260604.119) surveys the landscape of data structures for representing and querying k-mer sets across large collections of sequencing datasets, classifying approaches by their supported operations and space-time trade-offs.

The minimizer concept, born from a 2004 paper on sequence comparison, has become one of the most influential ideas in bioinformatics -- enabling tools like minimap2 and Kraken 2 that process data at scales unimaginable two decades ago.
